region.kaifeng.intro: Kaifeng is the Northern Song capital on the Bian canal and one of the largest cities on earth. Night markets stay open until dawn, grain barges crowd the canal, and examinations decide who will govern. But the steppe neighbours press from the north.
region.hangzhou.intro: Hangzhou on the West Lake is a city of silk, tea and canals. From 1138 it is the court of the Southern Song and grows into the richest city in the land. Teahouses, theatres and pleasure boats in town; hard labour in the rice paddies all around.
region.quanzhou.intro: Quanzhou is the great sea port of Fujian. Arab, Persian and Tamil merchants come here, the city has mosques and even a Hindu temple, and junks sail for Java and India. Sea trade brings wealth - and risk.
region.chengdu.intro: Chengdu lies in the fertile Sichuan basin, walled off from the rest of the country by mountains. Tea and rice grow here, brocade is woven, and the world’s first paper money was printed here. The mountains protect it - but not always.
region.beijing.intro: Beijing became a capital under the Mongols - Khubilai’s Dadu, the “Great Capital” - and the Ming later built the Forbidden City here. Winters are snowy and windy, the steppe and the Great Wall are close. A city of officials, eunuchs, soldiers and caravans.
